title: The per-tick gate must run a short suite, not the whole end-to-end suite
description:
The gate runs `go test -short`, but `-short` is inert: only 6 of 215 test files honour `testing.Short()` (12 call sites, mostly internal/cli/factory_test.go). So every per-tick gate runs the entire end-to-end suite.

That suite is not a unit suite. internal/reconcile has 206 tests and 8 time.Sleep calls — the cost is not sleeping, it is real work: each test builds real git repositories and spawns real subprocesses. Same shape in internal/exec/herdr (108 tests), internal/runstate (51), internal/cli (134).

Measured on the e9n attempt-8 gate (commit 46caa836a30c), 23 minutes wall:

    internal/reconcile   1363s   (~180s quiet, 7.5x)
    internal/exec/herdr   848s   (~176s quiet, 4.8x)
    internal/runstate     735s   (~113s quiet, 6.5x)
    everything else      ~290s   (~270s quiet, ~1x)

The packages that stretch are the ones doing real process work; the tests that FAIL under the stretch are the ones asserting on a deadline. That gate stopped the Phase 5 run on a herdr failure that does not reproduce on a quiet host (see e4u).

The fix is to make -short mean what it says: end-to-end tests skip under it, the per-tick gate becomes seconds, and the full suite runs on CI and at epic close-out where it is not competing with four concurrent gates. 6wh's caching stacks on top of this rather than substituting for it.

Operator, 2026-09-20: 'there has to be some bug with these very slow gates... We want to prioritize speed over very thorough gates' and 'this is a highly spec'd mac m5 with a few other things going on, unacceptable to have a flaky suite'.
acceptance_criteria: The gate command completes in under 90s on a quiet host with a warm cache, the full suite still runs on CI and at epic close-out, and the .tick/runners.toml gate stays byte-identical to the Makefile recipe so TestTheGateTargetMatchesTheDeclaredGate holds
